explain.say: See the clock? Waiting is hard. Yuki's legs want to rush ahead. She feels frustrated, which means cross and stuck. Lots of people feel that when they wait. Do you find waiting hard?

explain.say: Look at this line. Five people in front of Yuki. Each hop back is one person going down. Five, four, three, two, one, zero. My turn! Wheee! Well done. Your challenge: count down next time you wait in a line.

faq.a: When you want something, your brain wants it now. Waiting means holding that feeling. It gets easier with practice and waiting games.
asks: Tell me about Waiting is hard

faq.q: Why do we wait in line?
faq.a: A line is fair. The first person there gets the first turn. Everyone gets a turn in the end.
asks: Tell me about Others wait too

faq.q: What can I do while I wait?
faq.a: Count the people, hum in your head, wiggle your toes, or play I spy. Waiting games make time feel shorter.
You can say calmly, Excuse me, the line starts back there. If it keeps happening, tell a grown-up you trust.

faq.q: What if the wait is very long?
faq.a: Ask a grown-up, How long will it be? Knowing helps. You can also take a few slow breaths.

facts: A line or queue means the first person to arrive is served first.
Counting down the people in front is one way to see the wait getting shorter.

quiz.say: Five people are in front of you. Two have a turn. How many are in front now?
quiz.show: Five in front, two go. How many now?
quiz.why: Five take away two is three. Three more people, then your turn.

wrong.1: Seven is adding. People are leaving, so take away.
wrong.2: Two people went. Three are still in front.

quiz.say: Which is a good waiting game?
quiz.show: Which is a good waiting game?
quiz.why: Counting keeps your brain busy and shows the line getting shorter.

wrong.1: Pushing in is not fair to others.
wrong.2: Shouting can upset people and does not make it faster.
